in which sustainable diets have been measured in the existing literature. In a systematic review conducted in 2016, 73% of papers
focused on environmental outcomes, with less than a third focused on social or economic outcomes (Jones et al., 2016). A review
conducted in 2019 found a similar pattern where the majority of studies focused on human and/or health outcomes, with fewer
than 15% focusing on social and economic outcomes (Eme et al., 2019). In addition, most studies have focused on high income
countries (Jones et al., 2016; Eme et al., 2019).
